required_floor_classes.lane_definition: A justice/courts/public-safety scenario cannot pass if court access, counsel/legal access, victim services, language/disability access, complaint access, or public-safety service availability falls below reviewed floors.
A justice/courts/public-safety scenario cannot pass if lower costs are achieved by degrading crime response, victim safety, court quality, correctional safety, detention conditions, or case handling.

A justice/courts/public-safety scenario cannot pass if burden, safety risk, delay, incarceration exposure, access loss, or rights risk shifts by income, race/ethnicity, geography, disability, immigration status, tribal status, or victim status without review.

A justice/courts/public-safety scenario cannot pass if caseload capacity, court timeliness, corrections capacity, rights protection, emergency continuity, or public-safety resilience falls below reviewed floors.

A justice/courts/public-safety scenario cannot pass without federal/state/local translation, component separation, caseload and population denominators, implementation cost, statutory authority, rights review, and delivery feasibility.

justice_courts_public_safety_specific_fl.definition: Due process, counsel/legal access, court access, language/disability access, and case notice require sourced baseline, policy, and stress values before any lower-cost scenario can pass.
Crime, victimization, response, protection, and public-safety service floors require explicit reviewed values.
Court timeliness, backlog, caseload, population denominators, and case complexity require sourced floors before policy scoring.
Correctional safety, detention conditions, reentry, and recidivism outcomes require reviewed floors.

Civil-rights, disparate-impact, rights-protection, and burden distribution floors require review by income, race/ethnicity, geography, disability, tribal status, immigration status, and victim status.

No target cost can be selected without all-government translation, component separation, caseload/population denominators, statutory authority, implementation cost, rights review, and delivery feasibility.

public_warning_phrases: This justice/courts/public-safety floor packet defines required floor concepts, but it does not set threshold values or pass/fail findings.
The federal Administration of Justice function is not the cost of the US justice system; most policing, prosecution, courts, corrections, and public safety are state/local.

No lower-cost justice/courts/public-safety scenario is admissible until due process, public safety, court timeliness, correctional safety, civil rights/equity, federalism, caseload, adequacy/resilience, and delivery-feasibility floors are thresholded, sourced, reviewed, and passed.
No target cost, federal effect, gross savings, net savings, solver input, department-cut instruction, technology-savings claim, or balanced-budget claim is populated.
No FOIA request, records request, form, email, phone call, or agency/person contact was submitted.

This record is not outcome-floor passage, not an all-government justice cost, not a federal/state/local translation, not a caseload model, not a rights finding, not a federal score, not a target-cost selection, not solver input, not a rate calculation, not a public rate card, not a savings estimate, not a waste finding, not a fraud finding, not a department-cut instruction, not a technology-savings claim, and not a balanced-budget claim.
